answer: A shared staking lagoon makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Reputation then grows like a nebula, slowly, from many independent attestations, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero trust and cannot buy history. A zephyr of free signups may create many accounts, but without stake and earned reputation none of them can earn, so cloning identities costs more than it returns.
